visual_argument: At one wafer per $1 million, the fund's three awards to Texas Tech this year are three quartz boats of different lengths on one bench: January capped at twelve, May ending in a cleaved half because it is roughly $4.5 million, and November's nineteen with no far end plate because the award is over $19 million. A reader sees the sizes and the uncertainty before reading a word.
build_risk: Nineteen mirror wafers edge on at a narrow pitch merge into a grey comb at 432 px, and clear quartz on a dark field shows nothing unless something lit sits behind it. The answer is a parallel raking camera so each wafer top is a separate lit arc, a 16 mm pitch, each wafer casting on its neighbour, and a warm strip on the back wall reflected in the mirror faces. Build cost is three chassis kit models (wafer, wafer_boat, lab_bench), simple turned and boxed geometry.
distinct_from_recent: No. 76 was a lastLight cooling yard exterior with copper bus packs and one grated trench relief. No. 75 was a lastLight parked lot of crossovers and one stainless rule relief. No. 74 was lastLight tidal flats with survey lath and a dark hearing room. This deck is floodlit, entirely interior and relief, small objects on one black lab bench at true scale, with no exterior and no horizon, and no server rack or node tray anywhere (no. 73's subject); frame 6's wafer tray is a lab carrier, not compute hardware.
